questions.q: If a paramagnetic bar is brought near a bar magnet, then it is
options: Attracted by both the poles of the bar magnet
Repelled by both the poles of the bar magnet
Attracted by the South-pole and repelled by the North-pole of the bar magnet
Attracted by the North-pole and repelled by the South-pole of the bar magnet
questions.explanation: A paramagnetic material is weakly attracted into a magnetic field regardless of polarity, so it is attracted by both poles of the bar magnet.

questions.q:
Pick out the WRONG statements about magnetic substances (χ = magnetic susceptibility) (μ$_r$ = relative permeability).
I. Substances with $-1 \le \chi < 0$ are diamagnetic
II. Substances with $\chi \gg 1$ are paramagnetic
III. Substances with $\chi \ll 1$ are ferromagnetic
IV. Substances with $\mu_r \gg 1$ are ferromagnetic
questions.explanation: Statements I and IV are correct. Paramagnetic substances actually have a small positive χ (not χ≫1), and ferromagnetic substances have χ≫1 (not χ≪1); so II and III are the wrong statements.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is true in respect of diamagnetic substances?
options: They are feebly attracted by magnets
questions.explanation: Diamagnetic substances have a small, negative, and (nearly) temperature-independent susceptibility, and are feebly repelled (not attracted) by magnets.

questions.q: A uniform magnetic field of strength $B=2mT$ exists vertically downwards. These magnetic field lines pass through a closed surface as shown in the figure. The closed surface consists of a hemisphere $S_1$, a right circular cone $S_2$ and a circular surface $S_3$ [hemisphere on top and cone below, joined at a common flat circular face $S_3$ of radius $R=10/\sqrt\pi$ cm, with $\vec B$ pointing straight down]. The magnetic flux through $S_1$ and $S_2$ are respectively
questions.explanation: By Gauss's law for magnetism the net flux through any closed surface is zero, so the flux entering through one curved part must equal the flux leaving the other; using $\Phi=B\pi R^2=20\mu Wb$ gives $\Phi_{S_1}=-20\mu Wb,\Phi_{S_2}=+20\mu Wb$ (this question was ambiguous and KEA awarded a grace mark to all candidates).

questions.q: The Curie temperatures of Cobalt and iron are 1400 K and 1000 K respectively. At T = 1600 K, the ratio of magnetic susceptibility of Cobalt to that of iron is
The torque acting on a magnetic dipole placed in uniform magnetic field is zero, when the angle between the dipole axis and the magnetic field is ____.
questions.explanation: Torque $\tau=mB\sin\theta$ is zero when $\theta=0\degree$ (dipole aligned with field), i.e. the angle itself is zero.

questions.q: The horizontal component of Earth's magnetic field at a place is 3 × 10$^{-5}$ T. If the dip at that place is 45°, the resultant magnetic field at that place is
Which of the following statements proves that Earth has a magnetic field?
options: The intensity of cosmic rays stream of charged particles is more at the poles than at the equator.
A large quantity of iron-ore is found in the Earth.
Earth is a planet rotating about the North South axis.
questions.explanation: Charged cosmic ray particles are deflected by the Earth's magnetic field and get funnelled towards the magnetic poles, so their intensity is higher there than at the equator — direct evidence of the Earth's magnetic field.

questions.q: Earth's magnetic field always has a horizontal component except at
questions.explanation: At the magnetic poles the field is entirely vertical (dip angle 90°), so the horizontal component is zero there.

questions.q: Which of the field pattern given below is valid for electric field as well as for magnetic field? (A) lines radiating outward from a point. (B) lines converging inward to a point. (C) concentric circles around a point. (D) dipole-like field lines (as for a bar magnet or an electric dipole).
questions.note: The standard answer should arguably be (D) the dipole-like pattern, since it is physically realised by both a real electric dipole and a real bar magnet, whereas static concentric circular field lines (pattern C) do not arise from electrostatic charges (electrostatic field lines cannot form closed loops) even though they do describe the magnetic field around a current-carrying wire.
questions.explanation: As per the KEA key, the concentric-circle pattern (C) is the field pattern accepted as valid for both fields; patterns showing lines terminating at/emerging from a single point ((A) and (B)) would require a magnetic monopole, which does not exist (as per KEA key).

questions.q: In a permanent magnet at room temperature
options: Magnetic moment of each molecule is zero.
The individual molecules have non-zero magnetic moment which are all perfectly aligned.
questions.explanation: At room temperature thermal agitation prevents complete alignment of domains, so in a permanent magnet the domains are only partially aligned.

questions.q: A paramagnetic sample shows a net magnetization of 8 Am$^{-1}$ when placed in an external magnetic field of 0.6 T at a temperature of 4 K. When the same sample is placed in an external magnetic field of 0.2 T at a temperature of 16 K, the magnetization will be
questions.explanation: By Curie's law $M\propto B/T$: $M_2=8\times\dfrac{0.2}{0.6}\times\dfrac{4}{16}=\dfrac{2}{3}$ Am$^{-1}$.

questions.q: In a permanent magnet at room temperature
options: magnetic moment of each molecule is zero.
the individual molecules have non zero magnetic moment which are all perfectly aligned.
questions.explanation: A permanent magnet at room temperature is below saturation, so its domains are only partially aligned, not fully aligned.

questions.q: Coersivity of a magnet where the ferromagnet gets completely demagnetized is 3 $\times$ 10$^3$ Am$^{-1}$. The minimum current required to be passed in a solenoid having 1000 turns per metre, so that the magnet gets completely demagnetized when placed inside the solenoid is
questions.explanation: The demagnetizing field needed equals the coercivity: $H = nI \Rightarrow I = H/n = 3\times10^3/1000 = 3$ A.

questions.q: A magnetic needle has a magnetic moment of 5 $\times$ 10$^{-2}$ Am$^2$ and moment of inertia 8 $\times$ 10$^{-6}$ kgm$^2$. It has a period of oscillation of 2s in a magnetic field $\vec B$. The magnitude of magnetic field is approximately
questions.explanation: Using $T = 2\pi\sqrt{I/(MB)}$: $B = 4\pi^2 I/(MT^2) = 4\pi^2(8\times10^{-6})/(5\times10^{-2}\times4) \approx 1.6\times10^{-3}$ T, which does not exactly match any option (the exponent in the options appears to be printed incorrectly); KEA awarded grace marks to all candidates for this question, and the closest intended option A is kept here (as per KEA key).

questions.q: Needles N$_1$, N$_2$ and N$_3$ are made of a ferromagnetic, a paramagnetic and a diamagnetic substance respectively. A magnet when brought close to them will
options: Attract N$_1$ strongly, N$_2$ weakly and repel N$_3$ weakly
Attract N$_1$ strongly but repel N$_2$ and N$_3$ weakly
Attract N$_1$ and N$_2$ strongly but repel N$_3$
questions.explanation: Ferromagnetic materials are strongly attracted, paramagnetic materials are weakly attracted, and diamagnetic materials are weakly repelled by a magnet.

questions.q: The strength of the Earth's magnetic field is
options: Varying from place to place on the Earth's surface
questions.explanation: The Earth's magnetic field strength and direction vary from place to place on its surface, as described by elements like declination and dip.

questions.q: Which of the following properties is 'False' for a bar magnet ?
options: It points in North-South direction when suspended.
Its like poles repel and unlike poles attract.
questions.explanation: A bar magnet does produce a magnetic field around it, so statement (D) is false; the other statements are all true properties of a bar magnet.

questions.q: A magnetic dipole of magnetic moment $6\times10^{-2}$ Am$^2$ and moment of inertia $12\times10^{-6}$ kg m$^2$ performs oscillations in a magnetic field of $2\times10^{-2}$ T. The time taken by the dipole to complete 20 oscillations is ($\pi \simeq 3$)
questions.explanation: $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{I}{mB}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{12\times10^{-6}}{6\times10^{-2}\times2\times10^{-2}}} = 2\pi\sqrt{0.01}=0.2\pi \approx 0.6$ s. Time for 20 oscillations $= 20\times0.6=12$ s.

questions.q: The susceptibility of a ferromagnetic substance is
questions.explanation: Ferromagnetic materials have very large, positive magnetic susceptibility, i.e. $\chi \gg 1$.

questions.q: $\chi_1$ and $\chi_2$ are susceptibility of a paramagnetic material at temperatures $T_1$K and $T_2$K respectively, then
questions.explanation: By Curie's law, $\chi \propto 1/T$, so $\chi_1 T_1 = \chi_2 T_2$ (= Curie constant).

questions.q: At certain place, the horizontal component of earth's magnetic field is 3.0 G and the angle dip at that place is 30°. The magnetic field of earth at that location
questions.explanation: $B=\dfrac{H}{\cos\delta}=\dfrac{3.0}{\cos30°}=\dfrac{3.0}{0.866}\approx3.5$ G.

questions.q: If there is no torsion in the suspension thread, then the time period of a magnet executing SHM is
questions.explanation: The oscillating magnet's time period is $T=2\pi\sqrt{I/(MB)}$, where I is moment of inertia, M the magnetic moment and B the field.

questions.q: Core of electromagnets are made of ferromagnetic material which has
questions.explanation: Electromagnet cores (e.g. soft iron) need high permeability for strong magnetization and low retentivity so they demagnetize quickly when the current is switched off.

questions.q: The magnetic susceptibility of a paramagnetic material at –73 °C is 0.0075 and its value at –173 °C will be
questions.explanation: By Curie's law $\chi\propto1/T$ (T in kelvin): $T_1=200$K, $T_2=100$K; $\chi_2=\chi_1\times(T_1/T_2)=0.0075\times2=0.015$.

questions.q: A susceptibility of a certain magnetic material is 400. What is the class of the magnetic material?
questions.explanation: A large positive susceptibility (of the order of hundreds/thousands) is characteristic of ferromagnetic materials.
